Three source files name `PlanLimits` in code. `src/config/plan-limits.ts` declares it, and the other two import it for type annotations. Every other match is a `getPlanLimits` / `usePlanLimits` call, a comment, a test title, or a string in the manifest generator, so none of those name the type.

- **`src/config/plan-limits.ts`**: declares `export interface PlanLimits` (line 13). It also names the type in `PLAN_LIMITS: Readonly<Record<PlanId, PlanLimits>>` (line 29) and in the return type of `getPlanLimits` (line 107). The new field goes into the interface, and every plan entry in `PLAN_LIMITS` needs a value.
- **`src/hooks/use-plan-limits.ts`**: imports `type PlanLimits` (line 9) and uses it in the return type of `usePlanLimits()` (line 14).
- **`src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx`**: imports `type PlanLimits` (line 16) and uses it in `BillingPlanCardProps.limits` (line 27).

Excluded:
- `scripts/build-manifest.ts`, `scripts/manifest-parts/domain.ts` and `corpus-manifest.json` contain `PlanLimits` only inside string literals used to generate documentation. They are not TypeScript source that names the type.
- `tests/config/plan-limits.test.ts` has the word only in a test title.

I made no edits, since this was an impact analysis.

ANSWER: src/config/plan-limits.ts, src/hooks/use-plan-limits.ts, src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx
